metadata.file_name: 61. Wang et al. (2022). Beating the odds: Identifying the top predictors of resilience among Hong Kong students.pdf
metadata.title: Beating the odds: Identifying the top predictors of resilience among Hong Kong students

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 Hong Kong microdata and restricts the analytic sample to students in the bottom 25% of ESCS (Economic, Social and Cultural Status), yielding 1,459 students, of whom 251 are classified as resilient. The dependent variable is a binary indicator of resilience based on reading achievement being in the top 25% among low-ESCS students. Although PISA is collected using a complex sampling design, the manuscript does not report applying PISA sampling weights or replicate weights in the random forest classification. Because the analysis is implemented with the R randomForest package and the paper does not discuss survey-weighted ML estimation, the most defensible interpretation is that the model was trained on an unweighted subset; this may affect generalizability and uncertainty quantification under the clustered/survey design.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2018 Hong Kong data and selected only socioeconomically disadvantaged students defined as being in the bottom 25% of ESCS. The dependent variable was then constructed as a binary resilience indicator: low-ESCS students with reading achievement in the top 25% were coded as resilient (1), and the remaining low-ESCS students were coded as non-resilient (0).

Teacher support in test language lessons

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Reading (Hong Kong; ESCS bottom quartile; resilience defined via top-25% reading achievement)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Random Forest: AUC = 0.81; Accuracy = 0.83 (95% CI [0.79, 0.87]). Ten-fold cross-validation with five repeats; feature selection via mean decrease in accuracy (MDA) and marginal MSE reduction after the 8th variable. Logistic regression (supplementary): Accuracy = 0.68 (95% CI [0.64, 0.73]).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading data for Hong Kong students restricted to the ESCS bottom quartile, the study leveraged meta-cognition (assess credibility), joy of reading, teacher-directed instruction, perceived difficulty of the PISA test, and sense of belonging to school (among other top factors) to classify students as resilient versus non-resilient, finding that the random forest achieved high discrimination (AUC = 0.81) and accuracy (0.83). This indicates that strengthening metacognitive reading strategies and intrinsic reading motivation, alongside more teacher-directed instruction and inclusive school belonging, may help socioeconomically disadvantaged students reach high reading achievement, though the cross-sectional design and unweighted ML estimation limit causal claims.

data.outcome_summary: The study uses PISA 2018 Hong Kong microdata and constructs a binary resilience outcome among socioeconomically disadvantaged students (bottom 25% ESCS): resilient students are those whose reading achievement falls in the top 25% (n=251) versus non-resilient (n=1,208), totaling 1,459 students. Missing values (0–11.9% across variables) were imputed five times using MCMC multiple imputation in SPSS, but the random forest analysis used only the first imputed dataset. A random forest classifier trained on 30 personal and social-contextual variables was evaluated with ten-fold cross-validation with five repeats; it achieved AUC=0.81 and accuracy=0.83 (95% CI [0.79, 0.87]). The top eight predictors were identified via mean decrease in accuracy and marginal MSE reduction, with two variables showing negative prediction (perceived difficulty and discriminating school climate). Because the paper does not report applying PISA sampling/replicate weights and the design is cross-sectional, the results support prioritization of correlates rather than causal effects.
